Generate presence/pseudo-absence dataset

Source: R/h3sdm_pa.R
h3sdm_pa.Rd

Combines presence hexagons with pseudo-absences selected from hexagons without presence records. Two selection methods are available:

  • "environmental" (default): pseudo-absences are stratified in environmental space. Hexagons without presence are clustered with k-means on their environmental conditions, and the hexagon closest to each cluster centroid is selected. This ensures pseudo-absences cover the full range of environmental conditions available in the AOI, reducing bias from spatially clustered occurrence records.

  • "random": pseudo-absences are drawn at random from the candidate hexagons. When n_pseudoabs is equal to or larger than the number of candidates, all candidates are returned, so the user can apply their own sampling or balancing strategy afterwards.

Usage

h3sdm_pa(
  pres_sf,
  predictors_sf,
  n_pseudoabs = 500,
  buffer_k = 1L,
  method = c("environmental", "random")
)

Arguments

pres_sf

sf Presence hexagons returned by h3sdm_pres().

predictors_sf

sf Full hexagonal grid with extracted environmental variables, returned by h3sdm_predictors().

n_pseudoabs

integer Number of pseudo-absence hexagons to select. If equal to or larger than the number of available hexagons without presence, all available hexagons are used (no clustering or sampling is performed). Default is 500.

buffer_k

integer Number of H3 grid rings to exclude around each presence hexagon when building the pseudo-absence candidate pool. Hexagons within buffer_k rings of any presence are removed before selection, preventing pseudo-absences from being placed in areas likely occupied but not yet recorded. Default is 1. Set to 0 to disable.

method

character Pseudo-absence selection method: either "environmental" (default, k-means stratification in environmental space) or "random" (random sampling). See Description.

Value

sf object with columns:

  • h3_address: H3 index of the hexagon.

  • presence: factor with levels "0" (pseudo-absence) and "1" (presence).

  • geometry: MULTIPOLYGON of each hexagon.

Details

For method = "environmental", the function scales all numeric predictor columns before clustering. Non-numeric columns and columns with zero variance are excluded from clustering. Pseudo-absences are selected as the hexagon nearest to each k-means centroid in scaled environmental space (Euclidean distance). If the number of requested pseudo-absences exceeds the number of distinct environmental conditions among the candidates, the number of clusters is reduced to that number, since k-means cannot create more clusters than distinct points. The clustering uses a fixed internal seed so results are reproducible.

For method = "random", sampling uses R's random number generator, so call set.seed() beforehand for reproducible results. When all candidates are returned, they keep the order of predictors_sf.

This function is designed to be used after h3sdm_pres() and h3sdm_predictors() in the following workflow:


pres        <- h3sdm_pres("Species name", aoi_sf, res = 7)
num_vars    <- h3sdm_extract_num(raster_stack, grid)
predictors  <- h3sdm_predictors(num_vars)
pa          <- h3sdm_pa(pres, predictors, n_pseudoabs = 500)

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
data(cr_outline_c, package = "h3sdm")
pres       <- h3sdm_pres("Agalychnis callidryas", cr_outline_c, res = 7)
grid       <- h3sdm_get_grid(cr_outline_c, res = 7)
num_vars   <- h3sdm_extract_num(bio, grid)
predictors <- h3sdm_predictors(num_vars)

# Environmental stratification (default)
pa_env <- h3sdm_pa(pres, predictors, n_pseudoabs = 300)

# Random sampling
set.seed(123)
pa_rnd <- h3sdm_pa(pres, predictors, n_pseudoabs = 300, method = "random")

# All hexagons without presence (to balance later)
pa_all <- h3sdm_pa(pres, predictors, n_pseudoabs = nrow(predictors),
                   buffer_k = 0, method = "random")
} # }
